scopeReview: SPS-6.B.1/B.2: land-extensive development, sanitation, climate adaptation, environmental accounting and energy; regional planning, brownfield reuse, growth boundaries and farmland protection evaluated by outcomes and distribution.
varietyReview: Four meaningful original stimuli: urban land/population account, parcel histories, sector-energy chart and regional additions table. Other applications test cross-boundary systems, embodied burdens, site reuse, farmland, adaptation and tradeoffs.
repetitionReview: Different measures and scales: land per person, potential contamination, sector totals/shares and regional flow of new additions. No forced attribution of growth to a boundary or assumed household displacement. Varied keys and complete explanations; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official framework and primary EPA brownfield/reuse scope checked. All scenarios and statistics original/hypothetical, not site certifications, copied figures, outside lesson imports or independent human review.

questions.correctOption: Land area grows 40% while population grows 20%, so land used per resident rises.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed land1.4,population1.2,land/person7/6,density6/7. Built-area definition consistent; not a proof of one spatial form or a direct ecological-footprint-area measure.

questions.correctOption: A, because past industrial use and possible contamination can complicate reuse; site-specific assessment informs the next steps.
questions.independentReview: Primary EPA definition includes presence or potential presence; no demand for proven contamination before brownfield classification. Hypothetical site review only, not a real safety clearance or cleanup specification.

questions.correctOption: Total use stays at 100 units, while transport’s share rises from 20% to 40%.
questions.independentReview: Independent sums100/100 andtransportshares.2/.4 verified. Same accounting boundary and no double counting supplied; no energy-to-emissions conversion without fuel factors.

questions.correctOption: Development outside the boundary increased more than inside; regional evidence is needed before concluding that growth was contained or identifying the cause.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed inside300−200=100/outside250−50=200. These are changes in annual additions, not cumulative stocks or household displacement counts; no causal claim from a single before/after.

questions.correctOption: Shared waterways and connected settlement systems can transmit effects across separate authorities.
questions.independentReview: No pollutant concentration, treatment design or health prescription. Focus is regional sustainability effectiveness rather than a claim that one institutional form always succeeds.

questions.correctOption: A local inventory may omit burdens embodied in goods produced outside the city.
questions.independentReview: Distinguishes territorial and consumption accounting without asserting all relocations have identical emissions or supplying an unsupported numerical footprint.

questions.correctOption: Site-specific environmental follow-up together with access, housing costs and benefits to different resident groups.
questions.independentReview: No statement that all brownfields contain the same contaminant, all reuse is residentially safe or a geographic indicator replaces qualified environmental assessment.

questions.correctOption: It can preserve working land and limit some conversion, while transport, housing demand and shifted growth still require regional evaluation.
questions.independentReview: Direct SPS-6.B.2 scope; avoids causal guarantees, farm-practice stereotypes and numerical emissions claims.

questions.correctOption: Temperature conditions and usable access across neighborhoods, including previously underserved areas.
questions.independentReview: General urban climate-adaptation concept, not medical advice or a fixed cooling estimate. Does not presume a shade project fully resolves climate change.

questions.correctOption: Evaluate mobility gains alongside flood exposure, service capacity and who bears the risks.
questions.independentReview: Hypothetical planning comparison, no real flood-risk classification, construction recommendation or health/safety clearance.

questions.correctOption: Observed outcomes can differ from aims because of implementation, behavior, regional spillovers and changing conditions.
questions.independentReview: Completes effectiveness focus with no claim that monitoring alone isolates causality or that every initiative fails its stated objectives.
